title: A background event drives the same toast contract as an operator-driven event, with indistinguishable output on the accessibility tree
asA: screen-reader user of a shipped rcf-lite application receiving notifications from server-side events
iWant: a toast that arrives from a background push to render with the same role mapping, one-shot announcement, and timeout floor as an operator-driven toast
soThat: my experience is consistent regardless of where the notification originated

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the sample-app fixture's `POST /__emit` endpoint or an in-page background dispatch, a toast surfaced with priority `info` renders in `[data-live-region="polite"]` with `role="status"` and a toast surfaced with priority `error` renders in `[data-live-region="assertive"]` with `role="alert"` (identical output to a toast surfaced through an operator-driven control). Both toasts record `data-shown-at` and `data-dismissed-at`; both dismiss at or above the six-second timeout floor unless clicked away.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a background event surfacing a toast
acceptanceCriteria.then: the priority-to-role mapping and the one-shot announcement match an operator-driven toast
